summary: This bill raises the annual books-and-supplies stipend under the Post-9/11 GI Bill from $1,000 to $1,400 and adds automatic yearly inflation adjustments using the Consumer Price Index starting in fiscal year 2026.

scores.thoughts: The bill directly increases the annual stipend for books and supplies under the Post-9/11 GI Bill from $1,000 to $1,400 and indexes future amounts to CPI inflation. This unambiguously expands federal outlays on veterans' education benefits.
The bill contains no tax provisions, rate changes, or revenue measures.
No provisions relate to health coverage, insurance, or medical services.
No provisions address firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration, visas, or border policy.
No provisions address reproductive health or abortion access.
The bill amends veterans' education benefits administered by the VA; it does not alter Department of Defense budgets or active-duty military spending.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related provisions.
While the bill expands a federal benefit, the program is narrowly targeted at veterans' education costs rather than broad welfare programs such as SNAP or TANF.
The bill increases federal education-related payments to veterans but does not address K-12 public schools, school choice, or general federal education policy.
No provisions relate to controlled substances or drug enforcement.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions.
By raising mandatory spending without offsetting revenue, the bill increases the deficit and therefore works against debt reduction.
No provisions address LGBTQ legal protections or rights.
No foreign assistance or international aid provisions.
No voting access, election integrity, or electoral reform provisions.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight provisions.
No labor, union, or employment regulation provisions.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
